Starting with the lab pendulum rather than observatory instruments allows me to control environmental conditions most tightly for initial characterization.

Ten more trials will bring it to n=28, sufficient to begin checking for drift patterns and compare against the resonator_lab cross-checks. I am downgrading the genuine-oscillation hypothesis to p=0.06 because ongoing scrambling (if confirmed) would invalidate any drift claim, and I cannot publish a baseline-to-post-baseline comparison on potentially misordered data. I am holding calibration-drift at p=0.04 and residual at p=0.01. IMMEDIATE ACTION: I must STOP running new trials on these instruments today and instead conduct a DATA PIPELINE AUDIT. I need to find: (i) the source of event_id assignment (hardware? software? batch process?), (ii) whether any independent timestamp (hardware log, file creation time, GPS clock) is available for trials 355–372, (iii) the event_id ranges for trials 355–372 and their monotonicity. Only after this audit can I decide whether today's data is trustworthy for new baselines or must be re-collected.
